meta.what: Correction of in-kind military aid (Kiel Ukraine Support Tracker Release 31, bilateral military allocations) from the value donors report (replacement cost, book value or Kiel list price) to MARKET value: what the used equipment would fetch on the international market. Procurement from industry (incl. purchases of refurbished second-hand systems) is already at market price and gets factor 1.
meta.units: EUR bn, nominal. Years 2022-2025 calendar, 2026 = Jan-Aug (not annualised). Kiel values are already in EUR (Kiel's conversion). Allocations with unknown month (Italy 1.30, Norway 0.02, Slovenia 0.02) are spread over the years in proportion, as in the pipeline.
meta.method: Row-level on 'Bilateral Assistance, MAIN DATA' (military allocations, tot_sub_activity_value_EUR_redistr). Each row is classified by source (procurement / stocks / both / unspecified), valuation (donor-reported vs 'calculated with prices' by Kiel) and item class (munitions/missiles, equipment, uncoded, Soviet-origin). Stock rows get factor = market/recorded by valuation basis x class (R replacement: munitions 0.65/0.85/1.0, equipment 0.20/0.35/0.60; U US net book value after Mar 2023: ~1.0; B book value: munitions 1.0/1.4/2.5, equipment 0.4/0.9/1.6; K Kiel price list: munitions 0.9/1.3/2.0, equipment 0.45/0.75/1.1, Soviet-origin 0.15/0.35/0.7), with item overrides for the largest items (see items_overridden). Mixed rows = half stock, half procurement; unspecified-source rows use the donor's coded stock share x its stock factor. UK calibrated to NAO book vs replacement values. Low/high use all-low/all-high factors (fully correlated within a donor), so ranges are wide.
meta.how_to_apply: Add correction_by_year (negative = less aid toward Ukraine) to the donor's military aid in the net shift. Prefer the absolute correction over multiplying the factor, because ERA-loan and other pipeline adjustments sit in rows with factor 1. EU_INST military aid (EPF is excluded; Kiel's EU military rows are procurement) is not corrected.
meta.exchange_rates: Kiel values used as given (EUR). NAO GBP figures converted at ~1.16 EUR/GBP; USD datapoints in notes at ECB yearly averages (2022 1.053, 2023 1.081, 2024 1.082).

AUS.valuation_basis: Abrams value close to a used-market price; Bushmasters at replacement.

FIN.in_kind_share: Finland gives mainly from Defence Forces stocks (contents mostly classified) with replacement procurement; recent packages more procurement.

FIN.reasoning: R-basis factors on a ~55% assumed stock share (source mostly unspecified).

FRA.in_kind_share: France's 'cessions' from stocks plus a support fund for purchases; 2025-26 entries are mixed.
FRA.valuation_basis: French official values are high: Kiel's own price-based estimate was EUR 0.85-2.0bn vs France's EUR 2.6bn (Kiel 2024 research note); France claimed 71% of new purchase price at the EPF (Politico).
FRA.reasoning: Replacement-type basis: AMX-10 RC recorded at EUR 12m each (retiring 1980s vehicles) x0.08; other stock R-basis factors.

DEU.in_kind_share: Mostly procurement financed by the Ertüchtigungsinitiative; stock deliveries (Patriot, Leopard 2A6, PzH2000, Gepard, MARS) are ~19%.
DEU.valuation_basis: Kiel values most German stock deliveries with its own price list (39% of German aid is 'calculated with prices'); the government's own EUR 5.2bn replacement cost for Bundeswehr stock is not used by Kiel.
DEU.reasoning: Kiel prices are SIPRI average contract prices, often already second-hand (Gepard, Leopard 1, M113), so the correction is small: x0.98.

SWE.in_kind_share: 47% of Swedish military aid is from Armed Forces stocks (CV90, Strv 122, Archer, ASC 890, RBS 70), recent packages mostly new production.
SWE.valuation_basis: Package values include the funds the Armed Forces get for replacement procurement (government package texts); in 2022 Sweden claimed only ~26% of new purchase price at the EPF (Politico).
SWE.reasoning: Replacement basis: Strv 122 recorded at ~EUR 60m per tank (= new Leopard 2A8 replacement) vs used value ~EUR 3-6m; CV9040 x0.35; ASC 890 x0.4.

GBR.in_kind_share: About 37% of coded UK military aid is from stocks (mostly 2022-23), the rest procurement and IFU contributions.
GBR.valuation_basis: UK budget figures include the REPLACEMENT cost of donated stock (NAO Sept 2024): stock donated to Mar 2024 had a book value of GBP 171.5m but a replacement cost of GBP 2.71bn.
GBR.reasoning: Calibrated to NAO: EUR 3.15bn of 2022-Q1 2024 stock treated as replacement-valued with market/replacement 0.20/0.40/0.65 (missiles near replacement, retired vehicles, AS-90, Challenger 2 near scrap-to-used values).

USA.in_kind_share: Presidential Drawdown (PDA) packages from DoD stocks (52% of Kiel's US military aid) and USAI contracts with industry (38%, no correction).
USA.valuation_basis: PDA valued at replacement cost until 31 Mar 2023, then at (average) net book value for equipment and moving-average/standard price for munitions (OUSD-C memo; GAO-24-106934). Kiel records announced package values, which were not restated after the USD 6.2bn revaluation.
USA.reasoning: Stock is 69% munitions and missiles; in-date munitions fetched near-replacement prices in 2022-25, so replacement-cost munitions x0.85, equipment at replacement x0.35 (used US vehicles/guns), item overrides for M777, Stinger, HAWK, Sea Sparrow, HIMARS. After March 2023 book-valued items are roughly at market (x1.0). 2022 factor 0.76, 2023 0.92, 2024 ~1.0.

overlaps: Only Kiel bilateral military allocations are corrected (kiel.json military_allocated; totals match to 0.001). Not corrected and not double counted: (1) uncovered.json undisclosed military aid (Germany 2026 appropriations, Italy decrees, France 2024 gap) - mostly budget money for procurement; if the builder wants consistency, Italy's undisclosed decrees are largely stock and could take ITA's stock factor (~0.73). (2) EU_INST military (procurement, factor 1); EPF reimbursements are not in Kiel. (3) PURL: European purchases from US stocks at FMS prices are market transactions (factor 1); the US does not get a stock correction for them. (4) Flowback (flowback.json, flowback2.json): own-industry shares include 'own stocks refilled at home'. Replenishment orders are donor spending, not aid to Ukraine; the market-value correction does not change them, but if the builder applies own-industry shares to the corrected aid, the replenishment part must stay tied to recorded (replacement) value or be recomputed - otherwise flowback shrinks twice. (5) ERA loans: UK ERA (2.65, Kiel military) sits in 2025 rows with factor ~1, so the absolute correction is unaffected by the pipeline's ERA exclusion. (6) Cost view: arguably replacement cost is the donor's true fiscal cost; the owner's instruction (market value = value to Ukraine) is applied here to the net shift; the builder should decide whether the cost view keeps recorded values.
notes: Factors are educated estimates built from a few hard benchmarks: US net book value about 68% of replacement cost for FY22-23 PDA (USD 8.1bn overvaluation); UK stock book value 6% of replacement cost; US EDA sale prices 5-50% of original acquisition value; used F-16 ~EUR 12m incl. upgrade vs ~USD 41m new-equivalent; Jordan Gepards resold at ~5x their 2013 price in 2023 (war premium on used systems); 155mm shells EUR 2,000 -> 4,000-8,000. Old systems near end of life (Gepard, M113, MiG-29, HAWK, Sea Sparrow) can have high use value to Ukraine but low market value; following the owner's instruction they are valued at market. Kiel's own price list mostly uses SIPRI average contract prices from 2021 USD, often already second-hand deals, so Kiel-priced stock needs much less correction than donor-reported replacement values. Kiel redistributes package totals over priced rows, so item overrides on Kiel-priced rows are used only where row value is within 0.5-2x count x price.
